title: fix: allow database rollback after WAL checkpoints
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes database and package rollback being refused when SQLite checkpoints already-captured WAL pages during Windows file-removal admission.

Related: #158163. Reproduces the failure reported by hourly run [36827062752](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36827062752/job/110255226021).

## User Impact

An interrupted update can restore its previous package after a checkpoint-only transition. Newer committed data, database replacement, and changed retained write evidence still refuse restoration. An exact reversal leaving committed bytes and retained write evidence identical is intentionally admitted: it leaves no later data for rollback to discard.

No schema, dependency, configuration, CLI, or service-lifecycle change is included. Auto-merge is off.

## Why This Change Was Made

The snapshot/restore owner previously hashed physical database/WAL layout. The Windows exclusive-removal probe uses SQLite's private WAL index; closing it folds the WAL into the main file and can delete the WAL while leaving disk SHM unchanged. The old guard classified that checkpoint as an intervening write and refused database restoration before package restoration began.

The probe remains unchanged because Windows requires its native handle to close before files can be replaced. It is the checkpoint trigger in this reproduced flow; the shared generation owner also needs to tolerate ordinary checkpoints.

The generation owner now checkpoints a verified private copy and hashes committed pages with the original file identity and retained WAL transaction counter/last-frame checksum. SQLite interprets journals and WAL frames. Physical-generation and SHM publication checks still fence capture.

The command fixture incorrectly replaced the isolated snapshot worker with raw in-process copies while native SQLite handles remained live. Closing those descriptors can release SQLite's process-wide POSIX locks. Removing that substitute restores real snapshot/content-version dispatch and deletes its path bookkeeping.

### Order dependence

On baseline `40d9ed0924dafa3ef1bf8cf604679e79aa33a3e4`, the interruption case fails alone but passes after the complete eleven-case prefix, ending with `settles native Windows task enabled state after update finalization (none)`. The passing full run captures an empty WAL; isolation captures four frames (16,512 bytes), which the removal probe later checkpoints. Neither selector alone, both selectors, either Windows block, nor the full prefix with either selector omitted masks the failure. No single masking predecessor was established, and cases do not share database files.

With the unsafe substitute removed, the old owner also fails in the full file (20 passed, 1 failed). The repaired owner passes the full file and isolation. The owner regression explicitly constructs the WAL/checkpoint transition and does not depend on incidental case ordering.

## Evidence

Final head: `8c64cac059357f18bd4271a0b97e4b7d832dc7d3`. Linux / Node 24.19.0; leases fetched that exact SHA and ran `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. No local tree sync, tests, or typechecks.

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| New cases against old generation owner | Checkpoint-only and exact-reversal admission fail as intended: 2 failed, 4 passed |
| Restore + seven owner/direct-import siblings, three runs | **111/111 each, 333 total**; command walls 226.59 s, 185.03 s, 205.57 s |
| Windows lifecycle file | **21/21**; 201.030 s summed test time, 238.94 s command wall |
| Original isolated Windows interruption case | Passed; 15.169 s test time, 22.85 s command wall |
| `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 40d9ed0924dafa3ef1bf8cf604679e79aa33a3e4 --head 8c64cac059357f18bd4271a0b97e4b7d832dc7d3` | **Passed, exit 0**; all 27 test typecheck graphs, core typecheck, lint, formatting, dead-export scans, and selected guards |
| Fresh direct-route Codex P1 review | **Scoped-clean**, with the accepted exact-reversal ruling included |

The first checker session did not deliver its completion result. Only the checker was rerun with SSH keepalives and streamed output; that run returned exit 0. The passing tests were retained without additional reruns.

The restore tests cover checkpoint admission, newer-data refusal, changed retained commit evidence, and intentional admission after an exclusive writer's exact reversal. Focused restore-file cost was 70.86 s command wall; final repeated runs spent 48.927–57.453 s in its tests. Real multi-database snapshots, exclusions, publication, and update-history preservation require the owner boundary rather than a pure comparer test.

### Accepted follow-up: warm snapshot-worker fixture

The maintainer waived the slow-file stop and approved one Windows-file run for this repair. An isolated case launches **72 synchronous snapshot workers**, consuming 11.948 s in those calls, with zero content-version workers. Disabling the optional admission cache changed neither the launch count nor the approximately 16.6 s profiled case time.

A shared warm snapshot-worker fixture is explicitly deferred, in the same cost class as #161867 and #162200. This PR does not reinstate the unsafe mock or add retries, sleeps, larger timeouts, skips, or weaker assertions.

Repeated-suite/checker lease: Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m3vebh0nn1f9awhh7p2f6s9s`, [run 36846053529](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36846053529). Windows proof lease: `tbx_01m3vd133djpjez0p4ezde3yxe`, [run 36843590852](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36843590852). All owned leases are stopped.

LOC: production +41/-8 (net +33); regression tests +73/-12 and support +2/-37 (combined net +26); docs +8/-2. Production growth reuses the existing private-snapshot owner instead of adding a WAL parser. Windows service behavior is simulated on Linux; no native Windows or published-driver installation test was run in this lane.
